records.title: Interventions to Reduce Burnout for Military Physicians: A Scoping Review.
records.abstract: Introduction Physician burnout is an increasingly researched topic, particularly since the COVID-19 pandemic. Burnout reduction interventions, both organizational and individual, have been studied in the civilian healthcare setting. Few have been conducted in military settings. A 2022 United States (U.S.) Department of Defense (DOD) Inspector General report identified staff burnout and fatigue as a serious concern for Military Treatment Facilities. Other studies identified a significant association between burnout and suicidal ideation. From 2011 to 2022, the suicide rates in the Active component of the U.S. military have gradually increased, and per DOD Suicide Event Report forms, workplace problems were identified as a significant stressor for 26% of those who died by suicide in 2022. Since poor outcomes, staff shortages, and increased suicide risk are associated with burnout, identifying interventions that reduce burnout are vital for military physician retention and our fighting force's well-being. This scoping review aims to identify and analyze all intervention strategies since 2018 that sought to reduce physician burnout in military settings. Materials and methods This literature search utilized PubMed, Embase, and the American Psychological Association's PsycINFO (APA) databases. Search criteria included the following keywords: "Burnout," "Physicians," "Military," "Interventions," and "Strategies." Eligibility criteria included studies after 2017 with pre- and post-intervention measures via a valid, reliable burnout survey method, like the Maslach Burnout Inventory (MBI) and the Professional Quality of Life Scale-5 (ProQOL-5), among physicians in a military setting. Results Database searches produced 84 articles for screening, but only three studies met analysis criteria. The first study evaluated an OBGYN training program's wellness component and reported no significant difference in burnout (MBI surveys) at 0-, 6-, and 12-month time periods. The second study was a 12-month randomized controlled trial (RCT) that evaluated the effectiveness of a Web-based tool at reducing burnout in behavioral health clinicians treating post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), using the ProQOL-5 to assess for burnout, and it also reported no significant differences between the intervention and control groups. Finally, the third study evaluated healthcare workers' self-reported stress levels pre- and post-utilization of a Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction toolkit at two Air Force Family Care clinics. This study did report a statistically significant decrease in both self-reported stress (P = .018) and burnout (P = .045). Conclusion Only three articles met evaluation criteria, illustrating the lack of evidence-based burnout reduction interventions in the military. Three additional studies did not meet eligibility criteria but offered promising interventions for further study, including a peer support network, simulations, and resiliency training programs. Further study of effective burnout reduction strategies in U.S. military healthcare settings is necessary to decrease personnel shortages, prevent suicide, and increase military physician well-being.

records.title: Randomised controlled trial to investigate an online compassionate imagery intervention for improving veterinarian mental wellbeing.
records.abstract: Background Veterinarians are at increased risk of psychological distress due to the regular experience of moral dilemmas, leading to compassion fatigue and burnout. This study explored the efficacy of a 2-week, modified online compassionate imagery intervention for improving veterinarian mental wellbeing. Methods A randomised controlled trial design was used with two parallel arms (intervention vs. wait-list control group). One hundred and sixty-two students and qualified veterinarians were randomly allocated to each arm. The intervention group watched a 10-15-minute video every day for 14 days to increase their self-compassion. Participants completed questionnaires to measure outcomes across four time points (baseline, immediately post-intervention, and 1- and 2-month follow-ups). Results One hundred and one participants were included in the analysis of variance. The intervention significantly improved resilience (F[2, 198] = 4.39, p = 0.014, ηp2  = 0.043), self-reassurance (F[2, 198] = 4.61, p = 0.01, ηp2  = 0.045), self-compassion (F[2, 198] = 8.80, p ≤ 0.001, ηp2  = 0.08), work-related rumination (distraction detachment: F[2, 198] = 4.92, p = 0.008, ηp2  = 0.047, problem-solving pondering: F[1.86, 184.82] = 5.88, p = 0.004, ηp2  = 0.056) and self-criticism (F[1.80, 136.94] = 3.60, p = 0.03, ηp2  = 0.045). These findings were sustained at follow-up and were associated with small-to-medium and medium-to-large effect sizes. Limitations Randomisation was not entirely successful. Due to missing data, an intention-to-treat analysis was not feasible, raising the possibility of an inflated treatment effect. Blinding was not possible due to resource constraints. Conclusions An online compassionate imagery intervention was efficacious at improving multiple outcomes associated with veterinarian mental wellbeing. These findings provide a rationale for developing and delivering compassion-based interventions to veterinarians.

records.title: A Randomized Controlled Trial of Social Support Intervention Effects on Stress and Burnout in School-Based Speech-Language Pathologists.
records.abstract: Purpose Social support is an interpersonal resource with established effects on reducing occupational stress and burnout. Unlike typically recommended self-care and self-awareness techniques, social support can be directly implemented in the workplace and serves as an effective buffer against job-related stressors. This study aimed to determine how social support influences reported occupational stress and burnout symptoms among speech-language pathologists (SLPs). Method We developed and implemented a social support group program called Peer Support for School-based Speech-Language Therapists, using a randomized control trial design. Forty-six school-based SLPs were randomly assigned to either an immediate or delayed treatment group and participated in weekly social support group sessions online for 6 weeks. Pretest, posttest, and delayed posttest scores on the SLP Stress Inventory and the Maslach Burnout Inventory: Educators Survey were compared. Results Changes across postintervention and delayed postintervention for the treatment group were observed. A significant difference was found between each time point for total stress scores and for emotional exhaustion scores. The mean total stress score was significantly reduced between baseline intervention and postintervention and then increased slightly at delayed postintervention. The data did not reveal significant posttest differences between the treatment and delayed treatment groups. Conclusions The positive feedback provided by the participants suggests that access to additional peer support can be equally important to the management of stress and burnout symptoms. Implications, limitations, and future directions of this work are discussed. Supplemental material https://doi.org/10.23641/asha.33989560.

records.title: Participants' experiences of living with cystic fibrosis related diabetes and using a hybrid closed-loop system to support self-management: qualitative study.
records.abstract: Background Cystic fibrosis-related diabetes (CFrD) is a common complication of cystic fibrosis (CF). Many people with CFrD struggle to keep glucose within target range leading to poorer clinical outcomes and reduced life expectancy. Hybrid closed-loop (HCL) systems are an exciting innovation which may help people with CFrD improve their glucose management and experience a better quality-of-life. We explored the experiences of adults with CFrD who used the CamAPS FX HCL to: understand the benefits and challenges to using HCL in people with CFrD; and, help inform decision-making about HCL use in CFrD populations in routine clinical care. Methods We interviewed 19 individuals who used the CamAPS FX HCL for ≥ 3 months during the CL4P-CF clinical trial. Data were analysed thematically. Results Participants reported multiple clinical and quality-of-life benefits to using HCL. Many described treatment burnout before using the system and, hence, benefitting from automated glucose regulation and an increased capacity to take on new activities. Participants also shared historical difficulties gaining/maintaining weight as a result of their CF and described how using the system helped them achieve weight/muscle gain, improved their bodily confidence and enabled to them to enjoy a greater diversity of foods. Participants also observed CF-related benefits, including a (perceived) reduced susceptibility to infections, improved mood/energy to take on CF management-tasks, and increased confidence and ability to undertake physical activity due to a reduced risk of hypoglycaemia. In addition, participants reported medical trauma arising from hospital admissions in childhood and exposure to medically-invasive procedures for their CF, and highlighted benefits to using a system which mitigated the need to use injections. Due to their earlier traumatic experiences, some expressed a preference for using tubeless pumps and cannulas that require less frequent replacement. Conclusions Participants reported improved glucose management, CF-related benefits and wide-ranging quality-of-life gains resulting from HCL use. Given their earlier experiences of treatment burnout and medically-related trauma, and taking account of the distinctive challenges involved in managing CFrD, our findings suggest that people with CFrD are a uniquely deserving group for access to HCL technology if shown to be clinically and cost effective in this population. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT05562492, registration date 28th September 2022.

records.title: Effectiveness and Implementation of a Multi-domain Workplace Health Promotion Intervention in Home Care: Findings from a Controlled Pre-Post Study
records.abstract: Abstract    Background  Home care workers are exposed to high psychological, physical, and social job demands. Evidence of tailored and context-specific health promotion interventions for this target group is still scarce. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness and implementation of a multi-domain workplace health promotion intervention to promote health and work-related outcomes among home care workers in Germany. Methods  Home care agencies were assigned either to an intervention (n = 6) or a control (n = 5) group. The intervention was delivered either as workshops or in a self-guided format. Effectiveness was assessed using standardized questionnaires, including work ability, health status, and intention to leave as primary outcomes, and burnout, psychological well-being, perceived work strain, occupational self-efficacy, participative safety, work-related resilience, and job satisfaction as secondary outcomes. Implementation was evaluated using Proctor’s implementation outcomes framework and the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research, drawing on quantitative surveys and qualitative data from workshops. Data were collected between March and November 2023. Results  A total of 71 home care workers in the intervention group and 31 in the control group completed both the baseline and follow-up surveys. No statistically significant between-group differences were found for changes in work ability, health status, and intention to leave. However, significant between-group effects were observed for occupational self-efficacy (b = 0.20, 95% CI [0.02, 0.37], p = 0.027) and participative safety (b = 5.08, 95% CI [1.66, 8.51], p = 0.004). In addition, descriptive within-group analyses indicated positive trends in the intervention group for work ability, health status, burnout, perceived work strain, psychological well-being, and resilience, although these did not reach statistical significance. Facilitators were predominantly identified in the innovation domain, whereas barriers were identified in the inner setting domain. Conclusions  This study contributes to fostering a supportive and empowering work environment in home care, even though effects on broader health and work-related outcomes were not evident. Implementation into daily practice and application of intervention content remained barriers. Future research should focus on strengthening implementation strategies, organizational readiness, and leadership engagement to enhance the effectiveness of workplace health promotion interventions in home care. Trial registration:  German Clinical Trial Register (DRKS00031949), 24 May 2023, Retrospectively registered.

records.title: Unmet needs and functional dependence predict burnout, health outcomes, and institutionalization desire among informal caregivers: a multi-regional path analysis study.
records.abstract: BACKGROUND: The healthcare system primarily focuses on patients without engaging with, supporting, or attending to the needs of informal caregivers. A small portion of the literature pays attention to caregivers’ physical health outcomes. This study aims to examine how care recipients’ functional dependence and informal caregivers’ unmet needs affect caregivers’ somatic symptoms, co-occurring chronic diseases, and the desire to institutionalize care recipients, mediated by burnout, using the Informal Caregiving Integrative Model. METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted by recruiting a random sample of 476 informal caregivers from 11 cities across four regions in Saudi Arabia. Data were collected through structured telephone interviews. Path analysis was used to test the hypothesized model. This study follows the STROBE checklist. RESULTS: Most caregivers were female, providing care for an average of 8.17 years. Unmet caregiver needs (β = 0.490; p < 0.001) and higher care recipient functional dependence (β = -0.161, p = 0.001) significantly predicted caregiver burnout. Burnout, in turn, predicted somatic symptoms (β = 0.656, p < 0.001) and chronic disease co-occurrence (β = 0.215, p < 0.001). Unmet needs directly influenced the desire for institutionalization (β = 0.172, p = 0.012). Both predictors indirectly affected caregiver somatic symptoms (β = 0.321, p < 0.001) and chronic diseases (β = 0.105, p < 0.001) through burnout. CONCLUSION: Caregiver burnout is driven by high care demands and unmet needs, adversely affecting caregiver health and increasing the likelihood of care recipient institutionalization. The findings highlight the importance of tailoring multi-level nursing interventions to support family informal caregivers’ needs. The study findings can inform clinical practice, standardize caregiver assessments, and focus on the needs of caregivers to provide them with support. Responding to burnout may protect caregiver health and help prevent institutionalization. Conducted in Saudi Arabia, it offers insights for healthcare professionals and policymakers in culturally similar contexts. CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

records.title: Healthcare leader perspectives on strategies to implement and sustain interventions that promote employee wellbeing and reduce burnout.
records.abstract: BACKGROUND: Burnout and psychological distress among healthcare professionals are associated with adverse patient outcomes, workforce turnover, and substantial costs to health systems. Although a range of wellbeing interventions have demonstrated effectiveness, healthcare organizations continue to face challenges in implementing and sustaining these programs at the organizational level. Understanding leadership perspectives on implementation is critical to informing effective, system-level approaches to clinician wellbeing. METHODS: We conducted a qualitative study using semi-structured interviews with senior healthcare leaders across the United States, including Chief Wellness Officers, Chief Medical Officers, and senior nursing leaders. Participants were purposively sampled to represent diverse health systems and professional roles. Interviews were conducted between March and November 2024, audio recorded, professionally transcribed, and analyzed using thematic analysis. An iterative coding process was employed, with investigator triangulation used to enhance trustworthiness. RESULTS: Twenty-one healthcare leaders participated in the study. Four interrelated themes were identified: (1) professional wellbeing was viewed as fundamentally dependent on organizational and structural drivers rather than individual-level wellness efforts alone; (2) visible leadership presence and frontline engagement were perceived as critical to the credibility and effectiveness of wellbeing initiatives; (3) implementation required ongoing navigation of tensions between heterogeneous individual clinician needs and organizational constraints; and (4) sustaining wellbeing initiatives depended on framing them in ways that aligned with institutional priorities, often through a business case emphasizing retention, cost, and quality of care. Leaders consistently noted that symbolic or individual-focused interventions were insufficient without addressing workload, staffing, and operational inefficiencies. CONCLUSIONS: Senior healthcare leaders view clinician wellbeing as a shared organizational responsibility requiring structural change, leadership engagement, and strategic alignment. Effective implementation of wellbeing initiatives depends on integrating interventions into existing workflows, addressing systemic barriers, and articulating their value in organizational terms. These findings underscore the importance of systems-based approaches to sustaining clinician wellbeing within complex healthcare environments. CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

records.title: "Either you feel bad and stay, or you're smart and leave" - perspectives from emergency department staff in Stockholm, Sweden.
records.abstract: Background Job attrition and burnout among healthcare staff is a substantial challenge for healthcare systems globally. Staff working in emergency departments (ED) face work environment challenges including moral distress. This study explores causes, consequences, and contextual dimensions of moral distress among ED staff. Methods A total of 36 healthcare professionals from EDs at two hospitals in Stockholm, Sweden, participated in the study. Seven interprofessional focus group sessions were conducted. These were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. Results Participants described providing care under conditions of limited resources and high demands. Drivers of moral distress included inadequate nursing care, futile care, ethical dilemmas, organizational barriers, experiencing team-related challenges and lack of control. Ethical challenges were particularly evident in the care of vulnerable groups, especially geriatric and palliative patients. Participants identified systemic factors such as organizational errors, long waiting times, insufficient staffing, and lack of hospital beds as contributors to moral distress. Reported consequences included worsened well-being, a negatively influenced self-image, delayed reactions, and emotional numbing. Some participants expressed intentions to leave their roles, alongside frustration and distrust toward the healthcare system. Conclusions Moral distress emerged as a persistent and normalized feature of ED work, percieved to be primarily driven by resource limitation. These issues need addressing on a policy level. In parallel, strategies to manage moral distress in the ED setting are needed. This has implications for individual healthcare workers' well-being and organizational stability. Clinical trial number Not applicable.

records.title: Navigating complexity: nurses' experiences in delivering holistic care to patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
records.abstract: BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a complex, progressive condition associated with substantial physical, psychological, and social burden. Holistic, person-centered care is central to effective COPD management, yet its delivery in outpatient settings remains challenging. Nurses play a pivotal role in providing such care; however, their lived experiences of delivering holistic COPD care within constrained health systems are insufficiently understood. AIM: To explore nurses’ experiences of delivering holistic care to patients with COPD in university-affiliated polyclinic settings, and to develop an inductively derived conceptual model of holistic COPD nursing care that may inform future research and practice development. METHODS: A qualitative study using an interpretive (hermeneutic) phenomenological orientation was employed. In-depth, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 20 nurses working in King Faisal University–affiliated polyclinics in Saudi Arabia. Participants had direct involvement in outpatient COPD care. Interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis following Braun and Clarke’s six-phase framework. Methodological rigor was ensured through reflexivity, member reflection, and audit trails, in line with SRQR guidelines. RESULTS: Four interrelated themes were identified: (1) Seeing the Whole Person Behind the Breathlessness, reflecting nurses’ efforts to address psychosocial and functional dimensions beyond respiratory symptoms; (2) The Weight of Invisible Care Work, highlighting emotional labour, compassion fatigue, and family mediation; (3) Holistic Care in a Fragmented System, capturing time pressure and system gaps that constrained care delivery; and (4) Striving to Do Right by the Patient, illustrating moral tension alongside professional meaning derived from small relational successes. CONCLUSION: Holistic COPD care in outpatient settings is a morally driven, relational practice sustained by nurses’ commitment but constrained by fragmented systems and limited time. Structural and educational support is essential to enable sustainable, holistic care and to protect nurses from moral distress and burnout. CLINICAL TRIAL: Not applicable.

records.title: Ethical dilemmas and decision-making in emergency and critical care nursing in Western Amhara region, Northwest Ethiopia: a multi-method qualitative study.
records.abstract: Background Ethical dilemmas in emergency and critical care nursing often involve complex decision-making that impacts patient outcomes, emotional well-being of healthcare providers, and team dynamics. Understanding these dilemmas and the decision-making processes involved is crucial for improving nursing practices and patient outcomes in this context. Objective This study aims to explore the ethical dilemmas and decision-making processes of emergency and critical care nurses, using the Four Box. Method ethical decision-making framework. Methods A multi-method qualitative approach was employed, incorporating in-depth individual interviews (IDI), focus group discussions (FGD), and case studies to capture diverse perspectives. Data were collected from 28 nurses working in emergency and critical care settings at Tibebe Ghion Specialized Hospital and Felege Hiwot Comprehensive Specialized Hospital through purposive sampling. The interviews and focus groups were audio recorded, transcribed verbatim in Amharic, translated into English, and entered into OpenCode software for analysis. Inductive thematic analysis method was applied to analyze the data. Results The study revealed several key ethical dilemmas faced by nurses, including balancing patient autonomy with beneficence, and the allocation of limited resources during crises, opioid administration for pain management vs. respiratory depression, and conflicts regarding informed consent. Nurses reported emotional and professional impacts from these dilemmas, contributing to moral distress, burnout, and ethical fatigue. Nurses emphasized the importance of interdisciplinary collaboration and structured decision-making frameworks to navigate these challenges. However, the lack of consistent access to ethics consultations and peer support during critical moments was noted as a significant barrier. Conclusion and recommendation Nurses encounter complex ethical dilemmas that impact their emotional well-being and job satisfaction. Effective decision-making requires applying ethical principles, adhering to guidelines, and consulting peers. The study reveals the need for improved support systems, including more frequent and comprehensive ethics training, better access to ethics consultations, and structured frameworks to guide decision-making in high-pressure situations. Clinical trial registration The study is not a clinical trial, a clinical trial number is not applicable.

records.title: Grieving Children' Death in an Intensive Care Unit: Implementation of a Standardized Process.
records.abstract: Background:   The grief that accompanies witnessing the death of a child puts health care professionals at risk of secondary trauma, burnout, and turnover when left unaddressed.   Objective:   Support staff well-being and promote resiliency.   Methods:   Descriptive implementation of a structured, peer-to-peer bereavement support program for intensive care unit (ICU) staff at a tertiary children's hospital.   Results:   Thirty-five virtual sessions were held over the period of one year.Through these sessions, participants shared perspectives and normalized reactions, and explored potential coping strategies. Post-session feedback surveys demonstrated the negative impact of a death on the personal or work life of ICU staff. Additionally, nearly all reported some level of burnout.   Conclusions:   The sessions were feasible and positively impacted staff coping and well-being. Barriers and facilitators to session attendance, as well as suggestions for improvement, were also explored. Implications for practice and future research are discussed. No clinical trial registration is applicable.

records.title: Burnout and Cardiovascular Risk in Healthcare Professionals During the COVID-19 Pandemic.
records.abstract: Introduction The objective of this study was to investigate the psychosocial and cardiovascular markers in healthcare professionals during the COVID-19 pandemic. Methods This was a STROBE compliant, blended exploratory study. Residents, staff physicians, nurses, and auxiliary healthcare professionals from both inpatient and outpatient medicine services were recruited using a planned random probability sample. The Maslach Burnout Inventory (MBI), Fuster-BEWAT score (FBS), and socio-demographic factors, as well as sleep quality, were studied. The correlations between burnout severity and cardiovascular risk were examined using multivariable linear regression models adjusted for confounding variables, such as sociodemographic and anthropometric characteristics. Results The regression analysis with FBS as the outcome showed a negative association between cardiovascular health and emotional exhaustion [Coef.(95%CI): -0.029 (-0.048, -0.01),  p  = 0.002]. The higher the emotional exhaustion the lower the cardiovascular health. Further, the model showed a positive association between personal accomplishment and cardiovascular health [Coef.(95%CI): 0.045 (0.007, 0.082),  p  = 0.02]. Emotional exhaustion was significantly positive correlated with REM sleep and light average (Spearman's rank correlation: 0.37 and 0.35, respectively, with  P   Conclusion The data from this study show that healthcare practitioners who are with burnout and emotional exhaustion have an elevated cardiovascular risk, however, causality cannot be determined. As an adaptive response to stressful situations, REM sleep increases. The findings of this study may be relevant in creating preventive strategies for burnout and cardiovascular risk reduction or prevention. Clinical trial registration [www.ClinicalTrials.gov], identifier [NCT04422418].

records.title: Factors associated with clinical nurse's mental health: a qualitative study applying the social ecological model.
records.abstract: Background The prevalence of burnout, depression, and anxiety among Chinese nurses was 34%, 55.5%, and 41.8% respectively. Mental health problems have significant impacts on their personal well-being, work performance, patient care quality, and the overall healthcare system. Mental health is influenced by factors at multiple levels and their interactions. Methods This was a descriptive qualitative study using phenomenological approach. We recruited a total of 48 nurses from a tertiary hospital in Changsha, Hunan Province, China. Data were collected through focus group interviews. Audio-recorded data were transcribed and inductively analysed. Results Four major themes with 13 subthemes were identified according to the social ecological model: (1) individual-level factors, including personality traits, sleep quality, workplace adaptability, and years of work experience; (2) interpersonal-level factors, encompassing interpersonal support and role conflict; (3) organization-level factors, such as organizational climate, organizational support, career plateau, and job control; and (4) social-level factors, which included compensation packages, social status, and legislative provision and policy. Conclusions Our study provides a nuanced understanding of the multifaceted factors influencing nurses' mental health. Recognizing the interconnectedness of individual, interpersonal, organizational, and social elements is essential for developing targeted interventions and comprehensive strategies to promote and safeguard the mental well-being of nurses in clinical settings. Trial and protocol registration The larger study was registered with Chinese Clinical Trial Registry: ChiCTR2300072142 (05/06/2023) https://www.chictr.org.cn/showproj.html?proj=192676 . Reporting method This study is reported according to the Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research (COREQ).

records.title: Developing a mindfulness program for pre-clinical medical students in Indonesia: a mixed-methods study on suitability and appropriateness.
records.abstract: Background & aims Medical students experience high rates of psychological distress, including depression, anxiety, burnout, and suicidality, due to rigorous academic demands. Mindfulness-Based Interventions (MBI) have demonstrated small-to-moderate effectiveness in reducing stress and improving well-being, yet culturally adapted and developmentally appropriate programs for Indonesian medical students remain limited. This study aims to develop and evaluate the Mindfulness Program for Pre-Clinical Medical Students in Indonesia (MPPMS-I) to determine its feasibility, acceptability, and suitability in addressing the mental health needs of pre-clinical medical students. Methods This study employed a convergent mixed methods approach guided by the User-Centered Design (UCD) framework which emphasized iterative development based on user feedback. First-, second-, and third-year pre-clinical medical students were recruited between May and July 2024. The study was conducted in three iterative phases, each involving different participant groups to refine MPPMS-I: Phase 1 assessed initial impressions and interest, Phase 2 evaluated program relevance and clarity, and Phase 3 gathered detailed feedback on individual sessions to finalize the module. Quantitative analysis examined participant characteristics, interest levels, program relevance, applicability of learned concepts, and instructional clarity. Qualitative analysis were analyzed using framework analysis to explore themes such as participants' first impressions, key lessons learned, beneficial aspects, daily integration of mindfulness practices, and barriers and facilitators to participation. Dual coding was used to enhance trustworthiness. Results Findings revealed three key insights: (1) a moderate and rising level of interest (mean range: 5.75 to 6.6), supported by qualitative feedback indicating increased engagement following iterative refinement; (2) The program was perceived as highly relevant to students' academic and personal challenges, particularly around stress, perfectionism, and communication; and (3) Participants reported a high likelihood of applying what they learned, such as mindfulness practices like S.T.O.P. meditation and journaling, into their daily routines.in their daily lives. Themes of relevance, practical benefit, and cultural fit emerged prominently in qualitative feedback. Conclusion This study suggests that MPPMS-I is a feasible, culturally appropriate, and suitable intervention for pre-clinical medical students in Indonesia. Participants found it helpful for stress management, personal growth, and improving communication. As the program remains in an early evaluative phase, future research should include a longitudinal pilot study involving clinical students and assess long-term outcomes. Integrating MPPMS-I into medical curricula could offer a sustainable and context-sensitive approach to enhancing student well-being and resilience. Clinical trial number Not applicable.

records.title: Short Video Addiction and Learning Burnout: A Meta-Analysis
records.abstract: Short video addiction and learning burnout are frequently discussed together, yet reported effect sizes vary considerably, leaving the overall strength of their association unclear. This meta-analysis aims to quantify the relationship between short video addiction and learning burnout, and to examine whether differences stem from how addiction was measured, how broadly burnout was assessed, or what educational stage the students were in. We will search databases including CNKI, Wanfang Data, Web of Science, PubMed, and ScienceDirect up to March 2026. Eligible studies must be empirical, measure both short video addiction and learning burnout, and report a zero-order correlation coefficient. Data will be analyzed using CMA 3.0 with a random-effects model. We expect to find a positive association between short video addiction and learning burnout, with substantial heterogeneity across studies. The findings will help clarify the overall strength of this relationship and provide implications for educational interventions across different school stages.

records.title: Mindfulness-based interventions for stress and burnout in K-12 teachers: A scoping review of randomized controlled trials
records.abstract: In many settings, stress tops teachers’ reasons for exiting the profession. Mindfulness-based interventions (MBIs) may be effective in alleviating burnout and stress among K-12 teachers. This study presents results of a scoping review on the impact of MBIs on stress and burnout in teachers, with a focus on randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Databases were searched in September of 2024 for articles published in English from January 2014 through September 2024. Eight eligible RCTs across Asia, Australia, Europe, and North America, were included. The MBIs typically lasted 8 wk and included practices like mindful awareness of breath, body scans, practicing loving-kindness, and compassion. The RCTs were of moderate methodological quality and included both face-to-face and online modalities. The MBIs were generally efficacious in reducing stress and burnout, although burnout was less frequently assessed. They also improved some facets of mindfulness such as non-judging, observing, acting with awareness, and mindfulness in teaching, among teachers. Recommendations for future research and practice include incorporating objective measures (e.g. physiological indicators, administrative data); prioritizing longer follow-up periods to assess sustained impact; investing in more supportive teaching environments; and creating more compact MBIs by identifying the domains of mindfulness particularly relevant to teacher stress and burnout.

records.title: Factors influencing implementation of a digital compassion training program: Findings from a Randomized Waitlist-Controlled Trial (Preprint)
records.abstract: BACKGROUND Digital mental health interventions are increasingly used to address stress, burnout, and well-being among working adults because they offer scalable and accessible approaches to psychological support. Although digitally delivered compassion training programs show promise, implementation outcomes such as feasibility, acceptability, and participant-perceived fit remain underexamined. In particular, little is known about the extent to which digital compassion interventions help participants achieve the outcomes they most hope to gain through participation. OBJECTIVE This study evaluated the feasibility, acceptability, and expectation-outcome alignment of Compassion U, a blended care adaptation of Cognitively Based Compassion Training (CBCT®) program tailored for healthcare, education, and business professionals. Exploratory analyses examined potential signals of change in compassion-related and well-being outcomes. METHODS A pilot randomized waitlist-controlled trial was conducted with 137 participants from healthcare (n=46), business (n=54), and education (n=37) professions. Participants were randomized to either Compassion U or a waitlist control condition. The intervention combined asynchronous mobile-accessible CBCT modules with weekly live instructor-facilitated sessions over 10 weeks. Primary implementation outcomes included feasibility, acceptability assessed using the Theoretical Framework of Acceptability (TFA), and expectation-outcome alignment. Expectation fulfillment was quantified using a novel Expectation Fulfillment Index (EFI), representing the proportion of participants’ desired baseline outcomes subsequently perceived as having benefited from the intervention. Exploratory outcome analyses examined compassion, well-being, loneliness, stress, emotion regulation, and workplace-related outcomes. RESULTS Feasibility was supported by successful recruitment across all three professional sectors and retention rates comparable to those reported in digital mental health intervention studies. Participants demonstrated high baseline readiness to engage with the intervention, with no significant readiness differences observed across sectors. Acceptability was high at postintervention (overall acceptability score: mean 4.33/5) and remained favorable at follow-up. Participants reported broadly positive perceived benefits across domains. The mean EFI was 0.58 (SD 0.41); however, expectation fulfillment was highly heterogeneous, with 30.6% of participants reporting high benefits to desired outcomes and 27.8% reporting no benefits. Personal growth, self-compassion, and mental health were among the most frequently endorsed desired outcomes, whereas professional development demonstrated the largest expectation-benefit gap. Expectation fulfillment was most strongly associated with participant motivation and commitment to continued practice, suggesting that participant-defined goal attainment may represent an important but often overlooked dimension of success in digital mental health interventions. Consistent with the pilot nature of the study, exploratory effectiveness analyses identified 2 notable outcome signals favoring the intervention: increased beliefs in the malleability of compassion (Hedges g=0.70, 95% CI 0.26-1.13) and reduced loneliness (Hedges g=−0.55, 95% CI −0.97 to −0.11). Most other outcomes demonstrated small or negligible effects, and observed effects generally attenuated by follow-up. CONCLUSIONS Compassion U demonstrated strong feasibility and acceptability across healthcare, education, and business professionals and was perceived as beneficial in several domains prioritized by participants. Findings suggest that expectation-outcome alignment and expectation fulfillment provide useful participant-centered indicators of intervention fit and participant-defined goal attainment that complement traditional implementation and effectiveness outcomes. The association between expectation fulfillment and participant motivation further suggests that intervention success may be shaped not only by program use, but also by the extent to which participants remain invested in personally meaningful goals. Future fully powered trials should further evaluate expectation fulfillment as a participant-centered lens for understanding how individuals experience and evaluate digital mental health interventions.

records.title: Effect of Virtual Reality Relaxation on Alarm Fatigue and Professional Quality of Life Among Nurses in Intensive Care Units
records.abstract: ABSTRACT Introduction Intensive care unit nurses are faced with a large number of equipment alarms daily, which can increase the likelihood of errors and threaten their professional quality of life. Today, the use of virtual reality to create relaxing experiences in stressful environments has received attention. This study aimed to determine the effect of virtual reality relaxation on alarm fatigue and the professional quality of life among ICU nurses. Methods This is an intervention study with a pretest‐posttest design with a control group. ICU nurses who met the inclusion criteria were selected conveniently and were randomly assigned to two intervention and control groups (30 people in each group). The intervention was implemented as three 20‐min virtual reality relaxation sessions over a week. The data collection tools included the Alarm Fatigue Scale (AFS) and the Professional Quality of Life (ProQOL) questionnaire. The questionnaires were completed before and immediately after the intervention. Results The results showed that the mean AFS score improved significantly after the intervention ( p < 0.001), and there was a significant difference between the intervention and control groups ( p = 0.014). The mean dimensions of ProQOL also improved significantly in all three dimensions of compassion satisfaction, burnout, and secondary trauma stress after the intervention ( p < 0.001). There was a significant difference between two groups in all dimensions after the intervention ( p < 0.001). Conclusion The significant improvement in AFS and ProQOL scores indicates that the use of new technologies, such as virtual reality can be considered as a complementary tool in promoting the mental and professional health of nurses in stressful environments.

records.title: Does learning burnout link physical exercise and problematic short-video use? Evidence from a three-wave random-intercept cross-lagged panel model and supplementary machine-learning analysis among Chinese high school students
records.abstract: Background Problematic short-video use has become a growing behavioral health concern among adolescents, yet its longitudinal links with physical exercise and learning burnout remain insufficiently understood. This study examined the within-person bidirectional associations among physical exercise, learning burnout, and problematic short-video use, tested whether learning burnout served as a longitudinal pathway linking physical exercise to later problematic short-video use, and explored the predictive value of these variables for subsequent problematic short-video use. Methods A three-wave longitudinal survey with 6-month intervals was conducted among 1,327 students aged 16–18 years from five high schools in Yunnan Province, China. Physical exercise, learning burnout, and problematic short-video use were assessed using the Physical Activity Rating Scale-3 (PARS-3), the Adolescent Student Burnout Inventory, and the Short-Video Addiction Scale. Random-intercept cross-lagged panel modeling was used to separate stable between-person differences from within-person fluctuations while controlling for demographic and educational covariates. The longitudinal indirect association was estimated using 5,000 bias-corrected bootstrap samples. Supplementary ridge regression and extreme gradient boosting models, using nested cross-validation and a holdout test set, examined the incremental predictive value of physical exercise and learning burnout for later problematic short-video use. Results At the between-person level, higher long-term physical exercise was associated with lower learning burnout and problematic short-video use, whereas higher learning burnout was associated with higher problematic short-video use. At the within-person level, higher-than-usual physical exercise predicted lower subsequent learning burnout and problematic short-video use. Learning burnout and problematic short-video use showed positive reciprocal associations over time, and both predicted lower subsequent physical exercise. The longitudinal indirect association from physical exercise to later problematic short-video use through learning burnout was statistically significant but small. In supplementary machine-learning analyses, the best holdout R 2 was 0.311, but adding physical exercise and learning burnout did not improve prediction beyond prior problematic short-video use. SHAP results from the extended XGBoost model were therefore interpreted as exploratory feature attributions. Conclusion Physical exercise, learning burnout, and problematic short-video use showed interconnected longitudinal associations among Chinese high school students. Learning burnout may represent one small longitudinal indirect pathway linking physical exercise to later problematic short-video use, while recent problematic short-video use provides the most informative signal for future risk. These findings may inform the development and evaluation of school-based health-promotion strategies that support physical exercise, address learning burnout, and respond to recent problematic-use symptoms.

records.title: Explainable AI for resource-aware intervention prioritization of digital burnout in healthcare workplaces
MULTI LABEL KLASIFIKASI UNTUK PREDIKSI DEPRESSION, ANXIETY, DAN BURNOUT MENGGUNAKAN RANDOM FOREST
records.abstract: Peningkatan aktivitas digital, tekanan akademik, serta pola hidup yang kurang seimbang menjadi faktor yang berkontribusi terhadap munculnya gangguan kesehatan mental seperti depression, anxiety, dan burnout. Ketiga kondisi tersebut dapat muncul secara bersamaan sehingga diperlukan pendekatan klasifikasi yang mampu melakukan prediksi multi kondisi dalam satu proses analisis. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk membangun model prediksi kesehatan mental menggunakan pendekatan multi label classification dengan algoritma Random Forest. Dataset penelitian menggunakan 2.000 data dengan variabel aktivitas dan gaya hidup yang terdiri dari stress level, daily screen time, social media usage, age, dan sleep hours. Proses penelitian dilakukan menggunakan framework CRISP-DM melalui tahapan data understanding, preprocessing, modeling, dan evaluation. Pada tahap preprocessing dilakukan rekonstruksi label menggunakan weighted risk score dan penambahan kombinasi variabel berbasis pola perilaku untuk meningkatkan kemampuan diskriminasi model. Evaluasi model dilakukan menggunakan metrik subset accuracy, hamming accuracy, serta F1-score untuk mengukur performa klasifikasi multi label yang dihasilkan. Hasil pengujian menunjukkan bahwa model Random Forest memperoleh subset accuracy sebesar 85,75%, hamming accuracy sebesar 94,08%, serta micro F1-score dan macro F1-score sebesar 94,08%. Selain itu, akurasi pada masing-masing label menunjukkan nilai sebesar 93,25% untuk depression, 94,75% untuk anxiety, dan 94,25% untuk burnout. Hasil tersebut menunjukkan bahwa algoritma Random Forest mampu melakukan klasifikasi multi label terhadap kondisi kesehatan mental berdasarkan pola aktivitas harian individu, dengan performa label Anxiety (akurasi 94,75%, F1-score 94,71%), Burnout (akurasi 94,25%, F1-score 94,21%), dan Depression (akurasi 93,25%, F1-score 93,33%). Validasi silang 5-fold menghasilkan rata-rata akurasi 94,25%

records.title: Operationalizing decentralized clinical trials (DCTs) in community oncology: A thematic analysis of expert roundtable discussions.
records.abstract: 102 Background: Despite growing interest in decentralized clinical trial (DCT) methods, oncology research programs face operational, regulatory, and workforce-related barriers that may limit implementation. To better understand those challenges, the Association of Cancer Care Centers (ACCC’s) Community Oncology Research Institute (ACORI) convened a multi-stakeholder summit to identify and prioritize barriers to DCT adoption in oncology care settings. Methods: ACORI, in partnership with the Decentralized Trials & Research Alliance (DTRA), launched a structured roundtable series to identify real-world barriers and develop scalable, practice-informed solutions. Three expert roundtables convened between November 2025 and April 2026, bringing together stakeholders from academic centers, community oncology programs, industry sponsors, federal agencies, professional societies, and advocacy organizations. Discussions focused on 3 domains: foundational barriers, real-world implementation models, and equity, scalability, and sustainability. Presenters shared. Discussions were recorded and synthesized into thematic domains through an inductive qualitative analysis. Results: Four major themes were identified, each with associated barriers and facilitators (Table). Across all themes, successful DCT implementation depends on aligned regulatory guidance, operational readiness, intentional workforce development, and equity-centered design. Conclusions: These findings will inform the development of an ACORI DCT Site Self-Assessment Tool and Implementation Playbook to help oncology programs assess readiness and operationalize DCT elements. ACORI will expand mentorship and peer-learning opportunities to facilitate scalable adoption of best practices across community, federal, and academic oncology settings. Barriers and facilitators to successful DCT implementation. Theme Barriers Facilitators Regulatory & Oversight Complexity Form 1572 requirements; local provider oversight; on-site monitoring mandates Role-based delegation documentation; technology-enabled PI oversight Operational Infrastructure & Workforce Readiness Sample logistics; interoperability challenges; fragmented technology Hub-and-spoke models; workflow mapping Equity, Access & Patient-Centered Design Geographic distance; limited awareness; reimbursement challenges Local imaging/lab partnerships; 45,000 patient miles saved Scalability & Sustainability Staff burnout; workflow complexity; ROI-focused evaluation Phased implementation; physician champions; Quintuple Aim metrics; implementation science

records.title: Supporting Emotional Self-Awareness Under Occupational Stress: A Human-Chatbot Interaction Study
records.abstract: Emotional self-awareness, the ability to identify and describe one's own emotional experience, is crucial for emotion regulation. Higher emotional self-awareness has been associated with lower levels of stress, anxiety, and psychological distress. For healthcare workers, this ability may be particularly important because their work often involves repeated exposure to emotionally demanding situations, including heavy workloads, difficult patient or colleague interactions, and organizational pressures. In China, high levels of burnout and fatigue among healthcare workers highlight the need for accessible ways to support emotional processing and regulation. Cultural norms that place greater emphasis on emotional restraint may also make it less common to openly attend to and articulate distressing emotions. This study examines whether an emotion-focused interaction with a large language model (LLM)-based chatbot can help healthcare workers better understand and regulate their emotions related to occupational stress. Participants will be randomly assigned to either an emotion-focused condition, in which the chatbot guides them in identifying and exploring their emotions, or a control condition focused on neutral lifestyle topics. We will test whether the emotion-focused interaction improves emotion identification and description and reduces event-specific distress, state anxiety, and state stress relative to the control condition.

records.title: Social support effects on SLP stress and burnout (Marante & Hall-Mills, 2026)
records.abstract: Purpose: Social support is an interpersonal resource with established effects on reducing occupational stress and burnout. Unlike typically recommended self-care and self-awareness techniques, social support can be directly implemented in the workplace and serves as an effective buffer against job-related stressors. This study aimed to determine how social support influences reported occupational stress and burnout symptoms among speech-language pathologists (SLPs).Method: We developed and implemented a social support group program called Peer Support for School-based Speech-Language Therapists, using a randomized control trial design. Forty-six school-based SLPs were randomly assigned to either an immediate or delayed treatment group and participated in weekly social support group sessions online for 6 weeks. Pretest, posttest, and delayed posttest scores on the SLP Stress Inventory and the Maslach Burnout Inventory: Educators Survey were compared.Results: Changes across postintervention and delayed postintervention for the treatment group were observed. A significant difference was found between each time point for total stress scores and for emotional exhaustion scores. The mean total stress score was significantly reduced between baseline intervention and postintervention and then increased slightly at delayed postintervention. The data did not reveal significant posttest differences between the treatment and delayed treatment groups.Conclusions: The positive feedback provided by the participants suggests that access to additional peer support can be equally important to the management of stress and burnout symptoms. Implications, limitations, and future directions of this work are discussed.Supplemental Material S1. PSSST! Let’s Talk! lesson plans.Supplemental Material S2. Example of weekly newsletter.Supplemental Material S3. Procedural integrity form.Marante, L., & Hall-Mills, S. (2026). A randomized controlled trial of social support intervention effects on stress and burnout in school-based speech-language pathologists. Language, Speech, and Hearing Services in Schools. Advance online publication. https://doi.org/10.1044/2026_LSHSS-25-00114

records.title: Intensive Interventions for Burnout, Stress and Occupational Well-Being: A Critical Review and a Delivery-Format Framework
records.abstract: Intensive programs such as retreats and workshops are widely promoted for occupational burnout, but their evidence base is limited and fragmented. This critical narrative review searched PubMed, Google Scholar, and APA PsycInfo for peer-reviewed studies published from January 2000 to March 2026. Eligible studies evaluated structured, high-dose interventions delivered in a condensed format, reported burnout or closely related outcomes, and involved adult working or occupationally relevant training populations. Evidence was organized by four immersion dimensions: contextual containment, dose density, experiential multimodality, and social density. Forty studies met the criteria: 22 residential retreats and 18 non-residential intensives. No virtual synchronous program qualified, so adjacent virtual evidence was appraised narratively. Studies commonly reported short-term gains in stress and well-being and high satisfaction, but effects on validated burnout measures were less consistent. Most studies were small, uncontrolled, and drawn from healthcare and student samples, with little long-term follow-up; controlled trials yielded more conservative results. No study compared the same curriculum across formats. Delivery format may itself be an active ingredient, with facilitated social connection the best-supported candidate. Three testable pathways are proposed: contextual containment as a reset for exhaustion, shared group experience and communitas for disengagement and cynicism, and dose density as a catalyst for professional fulfillment and efficacy. Head-to-head format comparisons, standardized burnout measures, longer follow-up, and economic evaluation are needed.

records.title: Deep Learning-Driven Prediction of Academic Procrastination and Psychological Burnout: A Structural Equation Modeling and XGBoost Synthesis
records.abstract: Academic procrastination and burnout represent pervasive psychological challenges impairing cognitive functioning, academic persistence, and psychological well-being among tertiary students. While classical regression analyses demonstrate correlation between low self-efficacy and task avoidance, they fail to model complex non-linear interactions across temporal self-regulation dimensions. This study synthesizes covariance-based Structural Equation Modeling (CB-SEM) with supervised machine learning classifiers (XGBoost, Random Forest, Multi-Layer Perceptron) to predict chronic procrastination trajectories across a multi-institutional cohort of 1,420 university students. The SEM measurement model confirmed excellent psychometric fit (CFI = 0.964, TLI = 0.957, RMSEA = 0.041 [90% CI: 0.036–0.047], SRMR = 0.038), validating perfectionistic discrepancy, emotional dysregulation, and smartphone addiction as robust latent predictors of burnout mediated by active procrastination (beta = 0.48, p < .001). Machine learning benchmark comparisons demonstrated that XGBoost achieved state-of-the-art prognostic accuracy (AUC-ROC = 0.892, Precision = 0.841, Recall = 0.865). SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) attribution identified bedtime smartphone scrolling and perfectionistic anxiety as the primary drivers of next-day academic avoidance. || Akademik erteleme davranışı ve tükenmişlik, yükseköğretim öğrencilerinin bilişsel işlevselliğini, akademik sebatını ve psikolojik iyi oluşunu zedeleyen yaygın psikolojik sorunlardır. Bu çalışma, 1.420 üniversite öğrencisinden oluşan çok kurumlu bir grupta kronik erteleme gidişatını öngörmek amacıyla Kovaryans Tabanlı Yapısal Eşitlik Modellemesi (CB-SEM) ile denetimli makine öğrenmesi sınıflandırıcılarını (XGBoost, Random Forest, Multi-Layer Perceptron) sentezlemektedir. SEM ölçüm modeli mükemmel psikometrik uyum sağlamış; mükemmeliyetçi uyumsuzluk, duygusal düzensizlik ve akıllı telefon bağımlılığının tükenmişliğin güçlü örtük yordayıcıları olduğunu doğrulamıştır. Makine öğrenimi kıyaslamaları, XGBoost'un yüksek prognostik doğruluk elde ettiğini kanıtlamıştır (AUC-ROC = 0.892). SHAP analizi, yatmadan önceki akıllı telefon kullanımının ve mükemmeliyetçi kaygının ertesi günkü akademik kaçınmanın temel tetikleyicileri olduğunu ortaya koymuştur.

records.title: Occupational burnout in women schoolteachers in Kazakhstan: psychometric evaluation and psychosocial correlates within the job demands-resources framework
records.abstract: Background Teaching combines intense interpersonal demands with administrative and digital workload, and in Kazakhstan more than four fifths of schoolteachers are women, which makes burnout in this group a gender-relevant occupational health and wellbeing concern. Evidence from Central Asia remains scarce, and the performance of the Russian-language Maslach Burnout Inventory-Educators Survey (MBI-ES) in this population had not been formally examined. Methods In a cross-sectional study conducted between October and December 2025, 323 women teachers recruited by convenience in general education schools in three Kazakhstani cities completed the MBI-ES, the state scale of the Spielberger State–Trait Anxiety Inventory, and a structured questionnaire covering employment, workload, social-psychological, lifestyle, and digital factors. We split the sample at random, examined the structure in one half and confirmed it in the other, compared the three-factor model against one-factor, two-factor, and bifactor alternatives, tested measurement invariance, and fitted hierarchical regression models built on the job demands-resources framework. Results The correlated three-factor model outperformed one-factor and two-factor alternatives and fitted the validation subsample well ( χ 2 /df = 1.69; CFI = 0.955; RMSEA = 0.065; SRMR = 0.080). A bifactor model fitted better on global indices but yielded a degenerate exhaustion-specific factor and negative general loadings for accomplishment items, so we retained three factors. Loadings and intercepts were invariant across the random halves; across cities loadings held but intercepts did not. Subscale reliability was high (α 0.918 to 0.963). Job demands added 35.1% of explained variance in emotional exhaustion beyond background characteristics, resources a further 6.6%; perceived work stress, state anxiety, and low physical activity remained independent correlates in the full model (adjusted R 2 = 0.630). Depersonalization was associated with conflict, work stress, isolation, and an unfavorable collegial climate (adjusted R 2 = 0.443), and personal accomplishment gave the weakest model (adjusted R 2 = 0.170). Demographic and formal workload characteristics contributed little. Conclusion The Russian-language MBI-ES performs acceptably in women schoolteachers in Kazakhstan. In this convenience sample, burnout was associated more closely with appraised psychosocial working conditions than with formal job parameters. The cross-sectional design supports no causal inference, and the findings apply to women teachers in three urban settings.

records.title: Online Yoga Interventions for Stress Reduction: A Narrative Review of Evidence From 2017 To 2026
records.abstract: Background: Stress is a significant public health issue that is linked to psychological and physiological complications. Yoga is becoming an easy-to-access non-pharmacological method of stress reduction and has been identified as such in online yoga. Objective: To provide a narrative review of stress reduction from 2017-2026 across various population groups with an online yoga intervention. Methods: The narrative literature review was performed by searching the PubMed, Scopus, DOAJ, and other peer-reviewed databases. Studies were included if they focused on online, tele-yoga, app-based or digitally delivered yoga and measured stress, anxiety, psychological or mental health outcomes. Results: Evidence from randomized trials, pilot studies, feasibility studies, and systematic reviews suggests that online yoga may reduce perceived stress, anxiety, burnout, and psychological distress, particularly among students, healthcare workers, adults with stress, and individuals with chronic or post-COVID conditions. However, study designs, intervention duration, delivery format, and outcome measures varied substantially. Conclusion: Online yoga appears to be a feasible and accessible adjunctive approach for stress reduction. More standardized protocols, larger trials, quality appraisal, and long-term follow-up studies are needed.

records.title: The Relationship Between Positive Psychological Capital and Academic Burnout Among Grade 12 Students Approaching Public University Entrance Exams
records.abstract: Academic pressure ahead of the contemporary state university entrance selection is highly prone to inducing academic burnout, which is destructive to students’ mental health. This study aims to empirically examine the relationship between Positive Psychological Capital and Academic Burnout among 12th-grade students of SMAN 10 Semarang preparing for university entrance exams. This quantitative correlational study involved 127 12th-grade students selected via simple random sampling. Data collection was carried out digitally through online scales in the form of a 4-point Likert scale, adapting the Psychological Capital Questionnaire (PCQ) and the Maslach Burnout Inventory-Student Survey (MBI-SS). The results of the parametric statistical analysis using the Pearson Product Moment correlation showed a significant and very strong negative relationship between the two variables (r = -0.753; p < 0.001). These findings indicate that higher levels of students' internal positive psychological capital (hope, efficacy, resilience, optimism) are associated with lower levels of experienced academic burnout. School counselors are recommended to integrate positive psychology intervention programs to strengthen the internal adaptive capacity of 12th-grade students in reducing academic pressure.

records.title: A system for objective diagnosis of psychoemotional disorders and social maladaptation to assess the effectiveness of non-pharmacological interventions for healthcare workers prone to professional burnout
records.abstract: Objective. To develop and validate a comprehensive system for objective diagnosis of psychoemotional disorders and social maladjustment in healthcare workers with professional burnout, as well as to evaluate the effectiveness of non-pharmacological technologies based on original system. Material and methods. A prospective, controlled, randomized study involved 180 healthcare workers (28—62 years old) with signs of professional burnout. All patients received basic interventions (physical exercise and psychological correction). They were randomized into six groups by 30 participants each: control group (basic correction only), comparison groups 1—4 (basic correction plus one physiotherapeutic method: whole-body air cryotherapy, whole-body magnetic therapy, intermittent hypoxic-hyperoxic training or hydrogen therapy), and main group (basic correction plus all four physiotherapy methods). We assessed psychometric properties of diagnostic complex (reliability, validity, diagnostic accuracy), dynamics of professional burnout (MBI), anxiety-depressive disorders (HADS, DASS-21), somatization (PHQ-15), social maladjustment (SASS), and heart rate variability. Results. Original diagnostic complex demonstrated high psychometric properties: internal consistency (α=0.79—0.89), construct validity (CFI=0.94, RMSEA=0.058), diagnostic accuracy (AUC=0.92). Three clinical and psychopathological variants of professional maladjustment were identified: somatoform (32.2%), anxious-dysphoric (40.0%), and asthenodepressive ones (27.8%). The greatest therapeutic effect was achieved in the main group: integral index of burnout decreased by 31.0%, anxiety by 41.8%, depression by 46.2%, somatization by 43.4%, and social maladjustment by 33.3% (p<0.001). Combination of four physiotherapeutic methods significantly outperformed all monotherapy methods across all parameters (p<0.001). The combined effect is not a simple sum because we found supra-additive synergism (reliable change index 76.7—80.0% in the study group versus 46.7—53.3% in the comparison groups). There were significant correlations between reduced professional burnout and improved social functioning (r=0.68—0.72), as well as restoration of autonomic regulation (SDNN increase by 46.1%, LF/HF decrease by 47.5%). Conclusion. A comprehensive diagnostic system for psychoemotional disorders and social maladjustment associated with professional burnout in healthcare workers was developed and validated. Combination of physiotherapeutic methods (cryotherapy, magnetic therapy, hypoxic-hyperoxic therapy, and hydrogen therapy) effectively reduces symptoms of burnout and social maladjustment. Synergistic nature of physical factors was confirmed. There was a correlation between reduction of burnout and restoration of social functioning and autonomic regulation. This necessitates a comprehensive assessment of psychoemotional status and social adaptation when treating professional burnout.

records.title: Hubungan Dukungan Emosional Keluarga Dengan Resiko Burnout Akademik Pada Remaja Gen Z Di Lingkungan Sekolah Menengah Kejuruan Kesehatan Annisa 3 Bogor
records.abstract: Burnout akademik merupakan masalah kesehatan mental yang banyak dialami remaja Generasi Z akibat meningkatnya tuntutan akademik dan perkembangan era digital. Dukungan emosional dari keluarga menjadi faktor protektif yang penting dalam mengurangi risiko burnout akademik pada remaja. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengkaji hubungan antara dukungan emosional keluarga dan burnout akademik pada remaja Generasi Z di SMK Kesehatan Annisa 3 Bogor. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan desain korelasional dan metode cross-sectional. Sebanyak 110 responden dipilih melalui teknik stratified random sampling. Data dikumpulkan menggunakan kuesioner dukungan emosional keluarga serta Maslach Burnout Inventory–Student Survey (MBI-SS), kemudian dianalisis memakai uji Spearman Rank. Hasil menunjukkan 50,9% responden memperoleh dukungan emosional kategori sedang, sedangkan 46,4% mengalami burnout akademik pada kategori sedang. Uji Spearman Rank menunjukkan hubungan yang signifikan antara kedua variabel (p=0,000; r=-0,420). Nilai korelasi negatif dengan kekuatan sedang mengindikasikan bahwa semakin tinggi dukungan emosional yang diterima remaja, semakin rendah risiko burnout akademik. Temuan ini juga menunjukkan bahwa dukungan emosional keluarga berkontribusi terhadap tingkat burnout akademik, meskipun bukan satu-satunya faktor yang memengaruhinya. Oleh sebab itu, keluarga perlu memperkuat komunikasi, meningkatkan kepedulian, dan memberikan dukungan emosional secara berkelanjutan untuk mencegah burnout akademik pada remaja Generasi Z.

records.title: Enhancing neurodivergent student success through wellbeing: Protocol for a quasi-experimental evaluation of the Tuned In Connect program across three Australian universities
records.abstract: Neurodivergent university students face significant barriers to participation and success including sensory sensitivities, executive function challenges, social pressures, identity masking, and burnout. Evidence-based programs addressing the social and emotional dimensions of neurodivergent students' experiences are needed. This protocol describes an evaluation of the Tuned In Connect program, comprising an online self-paced module and a five-session group course. It was adapted by and for neurodivergent university students from the original Tuned In, an emotion regulation intervention that uses a two-dimensional model of emotion and music listening. Participants will be 145 neurodivergent students recruited from three Australian universities. The study will adopt a mixed between- and within-participants design, with participants randomly allocated to the intervention or waitlist control condition, and assessments at baseline and approximately six weeks later. Control participants will have the option of attending the intervention after their 6-week survey and will be asked to complete a third survey after the program. Historical control data from a 2023 cohort of neurodivergent university students may be used to supplement the waitlist control condition. Primary outcomes include sense of belonging, academic motivation, academic course completion, and semester grade point average. Secondary outcomes include emotion regulation, use of music for focus and coping, and wellbeing. Additional secondary and exploratory outcomes include anxiety, burnout, alexithymia and alcohol use. A qualitative sub-study will explore participant experiences through post-program focus groups analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. The findings, if positive, will support the adoption of Tuned In Connect by other universities as a scalable approach to supporting neurodivergent students. TRIAL REGISTRATION: https://www.acses.edu.au/trial/enhancing-success-for-neurodivergent-students-through-wellbeing-a-quasi-experimental-design-study-across-three-universities/.

records.title: A Systematic Review of Psychosocial Interventions for Enhancing Resilience in Medical Sciences Students
records.abstract: Sahar Ghanbari,1 Sara Hosseini,1 Sara Zamiran,2 Somaye Kavousipor11Department of Occupational Therapy, School of Rehabilitation Sciences, Shiraz University, Shiraz, Iran; 2Department of Occupational Therapy, School of Rehabilitation, Shahid Beheshti University of Medical Sciences, Tehran, IranCorrespondence: Sara Zamiran, Department of Occupational Therapy, School of Rehabilitation, Shahid Beheshti University of Medical Sciences, Tehran, Iran, Email saraazamiran@gmail.comBackground and Aims: Undergraduate medical sciences students experience substantial psychological distress due to demanding academic workloads and early clinical exposure, increasing their vulnerability to anxiety, depression, and burnout. This systematic review evaluates randomized controlled trials (RCTs) examining psychosocial interventions—including mindfulness-based programs, cognitive-behavioral strategies, acceptance-based therapies, and structured stress-management training—designed to enhance resilience among undergraduate medical sciences students.Methods: A comprehensive search of PubMed, Scopus, ISI Web of Science, ProQuest, Google Scholar, and Semantic Scholar identified studies published between January 2000 and April 2025.Results: 11 RCTs met inclusion criteria. Data extraction included participant characteristics, intervention type and duration, delivery format, and outcome measures. Methodological quality was assessed using the PEDro scale, and risk of bias was evaluated using the Cochrane RoB 2 tool.Conclusion: Across the included trials, psychosocial interventions demonstrated consistent positive effects on resilience, perceived stress, coping flexibility, and psychological well-being. Mindfulness-based programs—ranging from brief sessions to full 8-week MBSR courses—generally reduced distress, though shorter or peer-led formats produced mixed results. Cognitive-behavioral and stress-management interventions improved coping skills, emotional regulation, and self-efficacy. Acceptance and Commitment Therapy enhanced psychological flexibility, and structured resilience curricula such as the Penn Resilience Program yielded significant gains in resilience scores. Variability in intervention design, duration, and measurement tools limited comparability across studies. Overall, psychosocial interventions appear effective in enhancing resilience among undergraduate medical sciences students. Integrating structured, theory-based approaches into medical education may strengthen students’ psychological health and academic functioning. Future research should prioritize standardized protocols, culturally sensitive adaptations, and long-term follow-up.Keywords: resilience, psychosocial interventions, undergraduate medical sciences students, stress management, mental well-being

records.title: Can a Ring Measure, Predict or Heal Stress? A Critical Appraisal of the Oura Ring's Stress, Resilience and Cumulative Stress Claims
records.abstract: Background. Since 2023 the Oura Ring has offered three stress-related outputs. Daytime Stress labels minutes as stressed, engaged, relaxed or restored. Resilience grades the 14-day balance of stress and recovery on five levels from “limited” to “exceptional.” Cumulative Stress claims to reveal the “hidden toll” of chronic stress “before it manifests as fatigue, burnout, or illness.” Oura’s marketing invites users to “take charge of your stress” and “avoid burnout.” Its Chief Executive, in an interview the company filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), describes a device that can say “something’s really wrong” and prompt behaviour change. Objective. To define what stress and resilience are and how they are measured, to establish what a finger-worn photoplethysmography (PPG), temperature and motion sensor can physiologically detect, and to appraise Oura’s claims to measure, predict and help remediate stress against the published evidence. Findings. The ring’s inputs (heart rate, heart-rate variability, skin temperature and motion) index autonomic arousal, not stress. Arousal rises with psychological threat but equally with caffeine, alcohol, digestion, heat, posture, fever, dehydration, the luteal phase, many drugs and excitement. Oura itself acknowledges that the ring “can’t detect psychological stress.” Its own member data show that users who logged alcohol recorded about 50% more “stress” minutes, illustrating the non-specificity. No peer-reviewed validation of Daytime Stress or Resilience against a laboratory stressor, a cortisol reference or a validated resilience scale has been published. Cumulative Stress is supported by company-reported agreement with the Perceived Stress Scale or Copenhagen Burnout Inventory: 76% concordance in high scorers, 86% in low scorers and 82% overall. The development cohort, however, was recruited from people at the extremes of perceived stress, a design known to inflate diagnostic accuracy. The figures are not peer-reviewed and report no kappa, no calibration and no prediction of any clinical outcome. Resilience, a psychological capacity to adapt to adversity, is operationalised as a 14-day ratio of physiological load to recovery, partly built from a sleep score whose staging is itself weakly validated. On remediation, Oura does not claim to heal. We found no controlled trial showing that using the ring or its stress features reduces stress, prevents burnout or improves health. The study Oura cites tested a meditation app, had no control group and used the ring only as a measurement tool. Conclusions. The Oura Ring measures arousal, not stress. It labels resilience without measuring it, and it cannot predict burnout or illness on any published evidence. Nor has it been shown to heal stress. Interventions with evidence, such as mindfulness-based programmes and structured heart-rate-variability biofeedback, exist independently of the ring. Clinicians should treat ring stress outputs as unvalidated wellness indicators. They should neither dismiss distress because the ring is reassuring nor attribute medical arousal to “stress” because the ring says so. Keywords: stress; resilience; burnout; allostatic load; heart rate variability; autonomic nervous system; wearable devices; photoplethysmography; device validation; Oura Ring

records.title: Napovedovanje sindroma izgorelosti pri IT-strokovnjakih s pomočjo umetne inteligence
